_coverage: Script block content submitted to AmsiScanBuffer before execution
Deobfuscated, expanded content — includes decoded -EncodedCommand payloads
In-process cmdlets (Remove-Item, Invoke-WebRequest, etc.) — best coverage available
Context-aware rules: an entry with "requiresFlag" only blocks when that flag is
present in the SAME statement as the token. The base command is ALLOWED normally;
only the flagged variant is blocked. Examples below (normal vs blocked):
Remove-Item file.txt            -> ALLOW
Remove-Item dir -Recurse        -> BLOCK   (recursive tree deletion)
Remove-Item file -Force         -> BLOCK   (bypasses read-only/hidden protection)
New-Item path                   -> ALLOW
New-Item path -Force            -> BLOCK   (overwrites an existing item)
Set-ItemProperty HKLM:\... Name Value      -> ALLOW
Set-ItemProperty ... -Force                 -> BLOCK   (forced registry/property write)
Move-Item a b                   -> ALLOW
Move-Item a b -Force            -> BLOCK   (force-overwrites the destination)
Flags are matched on literal text, so alias/abbreviated forms of a flag are NOT
covered (e.g. -rec for -Recurse). See README known limitations.
BLIND SPOT: raw .NET reflection ([System.IO.File]::Delete()) that bypasses AMSI
BLIND SPOT: AMSI bypass techniques (out of scope for this ARCON)
NOTE: requiresFlag rules are evaluated ONLY on this (AMSI) layer. On the cmd.exe /
CreateProcessW / connection layers they are skipped, not applied -- put plain
unconditional rules (no requiresFlag) in global-policy.json / cmd-policy.json for those.
